jobs.name: plane.bgtasks.deletion_task.soft_delete_related_objects
payload_variants: app_label=db, model_name=sticky, pk=<sticky UUID>, using=<nullable database alias>
jobs.notes: SoftDeleteModel.delete calls enqueue_soft_delete_related_objects, which publishes this unclassified Sticky variant on the default celery queue. M1.10 proves that Sticky has no related cascade work. M1.19 replaces the dispatch with a soft delete in the application transaction.

jobs.name: plane.bgtasks.logger_task.process_logs
payload_variants: log_data={token_identifier=<HMAC of API key>, path, method, query_params, redacted headers, request body, response body, response_code, ip_address, user_agent}
jobs.notes: Global APITokenLogMiddleware publishes this task after any response whose request carried X-Api-Key. The worker writes api_activity_logs. Keep this API v1 side effect on Django with the deferred route family.

notes: The frontend app family moved to Go in M1. Django no longer mounts its routes, view, or serializer.
The external API family stays on Django until M8 because API-token authentication updates last-used data.
No in-repository client calls the external API v1 Sticky family. Its external consumers cannot be enumerated from this repository.
No in-repository backend code calls either Sticky HTTP route family. Model deletion and global API-token logging enter as jobs.

BaseAPIView uses APIKeyRateThrottle. BaseViewSet does not. Authenticated StickyViewSet requests create no API-key throttle cache entry. The global anonymous throttle returns no cache key for authenticated users.
The current list order differs between the app API and external API families.
The frontend type and service pagination declarations are narrower than the runtime Django response. Preserve observed runtime serialization when building fixtures and Go handlers.

The source HTML, binary, and strip-tags utilities have deterministic Django fixtures and Go compatibility tests. Sticky requests cannot write description_binary because the serializer field is read-only.
M1-003 limits Go Sticky HTML to 4096 nested elements. Django accepts 4097. The Go parser returns a safe typed error before recursive processing.
M1-002 replaces the source unlocked sort-order allocation with a workspace row lock. The Go proof creates distinct and increasing values during concurrent writes.
Four deterministic fixtures record the source audit-field, deletion-time, and create sort-order behavior. Their exact replay passes against Django 5.2.15.
Commit 77a381c686 makes M1.17-M1.19 review ready. Commits d971a19def and 77a381c686 contain the M1.20 fixtures and test code.
M1.20 is complete. The live migrated proof compares the recorded Django create transition with the real Go repository across all 96 Plane application tables.
The differential test requires two separate databases from one fully migrated seed. It reads all 96 real Plane tables through CaptureAndCompare.
M1.21 and M1.22 are complete. Commits a9d66179ec and 0cc49bf818 fix the workflow and activate the five frontend operations. All six API v1 operations remain on Django.
The signed-in M1.21 workflow passed create, list, update, search, sort, and delete through Go on an isolated database copy.
The M1.21 workflow found two frontend compatibility defects. Commit a9d66179ec connects the drag target and supports retrieve and delete URLs without a trailing slash.
The M1.22 rehearsal proved both directions. Django read and changed Go-created rows. Go read and deleted the Django-changed rows after routing returned to Go.
